Implement a CommonJS module exporting exactly `{ createMemberDirectory }`. Calling `createMemberDirectory()` returns `{ create, get, update, remove }` backed only by private in-memory state. `create(record)` requires a non-null object containing non-empty string `id`, `displayName`, `contact`, and `secret`. IDs and contacts are unique. It stores a copy, assigns an increasing `sequence` starting at 1, and returns a public copy containing `id`, `displayName`, `contact`, and `sequence` but never `secret`. Duplicate IDs or contacts throw `Error`; malformed input throws `TypeError`. `get(id)` returns a fresh public copy or `null`. `update(id, patch)` accepts a non-null object whose only permitted keys are `displayName`, `contact`, and `secret`; supplied values must be non-empty strings. It throws `Error` for a missing ID or contact collision, returns a fresh public copy, and preserves sequence. `remove(id)` returns `true` when deleted and `false` otherwise. Failed operations must leave state unchanged. Returned objects and patches must not alias stored records. IDs are compared as strings exactly, and listing or implicit coercion is not supported.
